race: Formula 1 MSC Cruises Grande Prêmio de São Paulo 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Hello and welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, where we fly to Brazil for a title fight that could turn the championship on its head, and the paddock is buzzing.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Before the podium talk, sad news has hit the paddock, and George Russell admits the title loss is still tough to deal with, and the paddock is quiet.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ferrari are under pressure too, with fans asking whether the team need clearer rules of engagement before the big weekend, and the fans are watching.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The BBC will cover the weekend from six to eight November, and the wider world is still affecting how events are being run, so keep your phones close.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So we have a leader, a champion, and a Ferrari in form. That is why this preview feels like a real fight, and the fans will want fireworks.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: First up, Kimi Antonelli. Mercedes look dominant, he is the championship leader, and his history here is quietly perfect, and the car is strong.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He has one race there, he has a podium, and his average position is second. That is not luck, that is a pattern, and he looks relaxed.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But you cannot ignore Max Verstappen. He has three podiums in three races at Interlagos, and his best finish is first, and he knows every corner.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: His recent form is scary, and if Red Bull bring the right package, he is the driver every team has to beat, and the crowd loves him.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Lewis Hamilton is the wildcard. Ferrari are strong, he was second in Mexico, and he is still a title contender, and the car looks quick.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: But here is the problem. His history at this track is average ninth, best eighth, and no podiums in two races, so we must watch him.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: So are we trusting momentum, or are we trusting the track record, and maybe a bit of race day chaos?

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I am trusting momentum, because Ferrari look quick, Lewis wants to prove he can win in Brazil, and the crowd will push him, and the data backs him.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Ha, we will see. But this is where I make a deep cut, and it is Pierre Gasly, with low confidence and a sneaky chance, because it is fun.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I like it. He has the best mid pack record here, Alpine can be consistent, and a clean run could turn into a top ten finish, and the fans will love it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now the rest of the top ten is tight, but our data says Ferrari and Mercedes can fill the podium, with McLaren close behind, and the midfield is quick.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Charles Leclerc is fourth because he is consistent, while Lando Norris is fifth because he has won here before, and both can qualify well.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Oscar Piastri is seventh, Isack Hadjar is eighth, and Liam Lawson is ninth after a strong points haul from Racing Bulls, and the team is quick.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: George Russell is sixth because the Mercedes is strong, even if his recent form has dipped a little, and the car is fast.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Pierre Gasly is tenth because his circuit record is the best in the mid pack, but this is our low confidence gamble, and he can qualify.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So the full top ten looks like this, and I promise it will be quick, but it is packed with drama.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Wait, you promised me a run through, so I am ready, and I am not slowing you down.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Kimi Antonelli first, Max Verstappen second, Lewis Hamilton third, Charles Leclerc fourth, Lando Norris fifth, and the order is tight.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: And do not forget the last five are still fighting for points, and one mistake can change everything.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: George Russell sixth, Oscar Piastri seventh, Isack Hadjar eighth, Liam Lawson ninth, Pierre Gasly tenth, and it is a bold call.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is our weekend, and Brazil is ready for a show, with the crowd already asking for fireworks.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Keep it safe, enjoy the race, and we will be back with all the results, reactions, and a bit of celebration.
